answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when independent audits confirm duplicate identities coordinating to claim rewards. Auditors compare signed action histories and shared funding or control signals, rather than treating an echo of similar wording as proof by itself. A relic of past good behavior may raise reputation, but cannot replace the stake or shield a colluding cluster. To multiply fake identities, an attacker must lock more capital and risk losing it, making a sable-colored swarm costly instead of free.
